title: Supply Resilience Playbook — Model Ops & Procurement Trigger Matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create an operational playbook and a deterministic trigger matrix that maps live signals (latency degradation, capacity shortfall, price spikes, model availability alerts, accuracy regressions) to procurement actions and Model Ops remediation steps. The goal is to reduce mean time to fallback (MTTF) for enterprise customers while limiting procurement spend leakage and preserving tenant isolation requirements.

Context: As open-model supply becomes more fragmented, large customers face outages or degraded experience when preferred model variants are unavailable or become cost-inefficient. This ticket synthesizes competitive market signals, runtime telemetry, and procurement constraints into a single operational artifact the SRE, Procurement, and Platform teams can execute from under SLA pressure.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Trigger matrix completed with at least 6 supply signals and deterministic actions (fallback model, region routing, reserved capacity toggle, procurement action).
A2: Cost/latency impact estimator validated for top 3 enterprise customers using historical traces and accepted by Finance + Solutions.
A3: Playbook runbook published in Confluence with run-through checklist and one tabletop exercise completed with SRE and Customer Success.
A4: GitHub repo with automation PR (infra playbooks + alert-to-runbook mapping) merged and deployment tested in staging.
spec:
Signals identified: token-latency-p50/p95, sustained queue growth > 3 minutes, model-variant-health-flapping, spot-instance-price-index > 30% baseline, KV-cache-miss-rate increase > 5x, accuracy-regression-alert per eval set.

For each signal define: detection window, severity bucket (S1/S2/S3), immediate mitigation, procurement action, escalation owner, rollback criteria.

Fallback bundles: define three bundles (Economy, Balanced, Enterprise) with model families, quantization profile, expected latency delta, and monthly reserved-capacity commitment.

Trigger rules: e.g., if p95 latency increases > 50% for > 10 minutes AND queue_time > 2 mins => route 20% of traffic to Balanced bundle in same-region, trigger procurement notification if Balanced reserved utilization > 85% for 2 hours.

Telemetry requirements: add new Console metrics: "supply_signal.index" (string tag), "bundle_utilization_pct", "fallback_traffic_pct", and an alerting policy that emits structured payload for automation.

Cost model: baseline_token_cost + delta = baseline_token_cost * (1 + reserve_premium) + region_egress_estimate. Provide simple CSV calculator and attach to Confluence.

Automation: create infra playbook that maps alerts to a GitHub Actions workflow which 1) patches routing policy, 2) notifies procurement Slack channel with templated message and estimated cost, 3) creates incident in PagerDuty if customer SLA breached.

risks: Over-automating procurement could trigger unnecessary reserved-commitments and increase costs.
Signal noise causing oscillation between bundles (risk of flapping).
Telemetry gaps in hosted model providers prevent reliable detection of model-variant outages.
Enterprise customers with strict model pinning may not accept automatic fallback — requires approval path.
notes: Reference: similar playbook scoped for storage provider outages (ops-incident-2025-11) — useful runbook template.
We should include a customer-visible incident template that explains fallback behavior and expected UX delta.
Procurement policy: any reserved capacity > $50k/month requires VP approval; include this as a gating step in automation.
